author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Ben Shelton knocked defending champion Carlos Alcaraz out of the U.S. Open early Wednesday, winning a five-set quarterfinal that produced the latest finish in tournament history.
Shelton prevailed 6-7(5), 6-1, 6-3, 1-6, 7-6(10-7). The match began at 11:05 p.m. Tuesday and ended at 3:33 a.m. after four hours and 28 minutes, Reuters reported.
The result sends Shelton into an all-American semifinal against Frances Tiafoe. It also ended Alcaraz’s 13-match unbeaten record against American opponents at Grand Slam tournaments.

The timing became part of the story as players and spectators remained at Arthur Ashe Stadium well into the morning. Shelton had to recover after dropping the opening tiebreak and again after Alcaraz forced a deciding set. The final tiebreak decided a match in which momentum swung repeatedly, leaving an American guaranteed a place in the men’s final. The United States has not produced a men’s Grand Slam singles champion since Andy Roddick in 2003.
dek: Shelton beat the defending champion in five sets at 3:33 a.m., setting up an all-American semifinal against Frances Tiafoe.
headline: Ben Shelton stuns Carlos Alcaraz in latest U.S. Open finish
